# 1\. What is High Availability

High Availability (HA) is a system design characteristic that ensures a critical service remains operational and accessible for the maximum possible time, minimising both planned and unplanned downtime. In the context of Oracle databases, HA is the foundation of any enterprise deployment where continuous data access is required.

## 1.1 Why HA Matters

Every minute a production database is unavailable translates directly to financial loss, damaged customer trust, and potential regulatory penalties. Modern HA strategy must address every failure domain - from a crashed process to a full data-centre disaster.

## 1.2 Downtime Categories

| **Category** | **Sub-Category** | **Examples**                                                    |
| ------------ | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Planned      | Maintenance      | OS patches, database upgrades, schema changes, hardware refresh |
| Planned      | Business         | Migration windows, batch jobs, application releases             |
| Unplanned    | Instance failure | Process crash, OOM kill, power loss, OS panic                   |
| Unplanned    | Data failure     | Block corruption, accidental DROP/TRUNCATE, logical error       |
| Unplanned    | Site failure     | Fire, flood, network partition, power outage to DC              |
| Unplanned    | Human error      | Incorrect DML, misconfiguration, wrong script on wrong host     |

## 1.3 Key HA Metrics

| **Metric**                        | **Definition**                                   | **Target (Gold tier)** |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- |
| RTO - Recovery Time Objective     | Maximum tolerable time the system is unavailable | < 30 seconds           |
| RPO - Recovery Point Objective    | Maximum tolerable data loss measured in time     | Zero (0 seconds)       |
| MTTR - Mean Time To Recover       | Average time to restore service after a failure  | < 5 minutes            |
| MTBF - Mean Time Between Failures | Average operational time between failures        | Years                  |

## 1.4 Availability Classes

| **Class**      | **Annual Downtime** | **Uptime %** | **Typical Solution**                 |
| -------------- | ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| Basic          | < 8.75 hours        | 99.9%        | RMAN backup, Flashback               |
| High           | < 53 minutes        | 99.99%       | Data Guard (Max Performance)         |
| Continuous     | < 5 minutes         | 99.999%      | Data Guard + FSFO (Max Availability) |
| Fault Tolerant | ~Zero               | 99.9999%     | RAC + ADG + GoldenGate + FSFO        |

# 2\. High Availability Solutions

## 2.1 Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture (MAA)

Oracle MAA is Oracle's prescriptive best-practice framework. It defines four tiers of availability, each building on the previous tier.

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ PLATINUM - Zero Data Loss + Zero Downtime │

│ RAC + Active Data Guard + GoldenGate + FSFO + Application HA │

├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ GOLD - Zero Data Loss, Near-Zero Downtime │

│ Active Data Guard + FSFO (Max Availability mode) │

├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ SILVER - Near-Zero Data Loss │

│ Data Guard (Max Performance) + Backup + Monitoring │

├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ BRONZE - Basic HA │

│ RMAN Backup + Flashback + OEM Monitoring │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

| **Tier** | **RTO** | **RPO** | **Key Technologies**                     |
| -------- | ------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Bronze   | Hours   | Hours   | RMAN, Flashback Database, OEM            |
| Silver   | Minutes | Seconds | Data Guard Max Performance, RMAN offload |
| Gold     | Seconds | Zero    | Data Guard Max Availability + FSFO + ADG |
| Platinum | Zero    | Zero    | RAC + ADG + GoldenGate + FSFO + App HA   |

## 2.2 Oracle HA Technology Stack

| **Technology**             | **Protects Against**                                | **Scope**              |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| RMAN Backup / Recovery     | Data loss, media failure                            | Single site            |
| Flashback Database         | Human error, logical corruption                     | Single site            |
| Oracle Grid Infrastructure | Instance/process failure; VIP failover              | Single node or cluster |
| Oracle RAC                 | Node failure, instance failure                      | Multi-node cluster     |
| Oracle Data Guard          | Site failure, media failure, data loss              | Multi-site             |
| Active Data Guard (ADG)    | Site failure + provides live read offload           | Multi-site             |
| GoldenGate                 | Heterogeneous replication; zero-downtime migrations | Multi-site/platform    |
| Fast Start Failover        | Unattended automatic failover                       | Multi-site             |

## 2.3 This Lab - MAA Gold Tier

This playbook builds a Gold-tier MAA configuration:

- Single-node Full Clusterware (Grid Infrastructure) on each site - gives VIP, SCAN, ASM without a second RAC node
- Oracle 19c CDB with 2 PDBs - CDBPRIM (primary site) and CDBSTBY (standby site)
- Physical Standby database with Active Data Guard - read-only offload on standby
- Data Guard Broker for automated management and role transitions
- Fast Start Failover (FSFO) with Observer for automatic unattended failover
- Max Availability protection mode - synchronous redo transport, zero data loss when standby is reachable

# 3\. Oracle Data Guard Overview

Oracle Data Guard is Oracle's primary disaster recovery and data protection solution. It maintains one or more continuously synchronised copies (standby databases) of a production (primary) database. When the primary becomes unavailable, Data Guard enables rapid switchover or automatic failover to the standby.

## 3.1 How Data Guard Works

PRIMARY DATABASE (CDBPRIM - lnx107) STANDBY DATABASE (CDBSTBY - lnx113)

┌─────────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────────┐

│ Application → DML/DDL │ │ Read-Only Queries (ADG) │

│ ↓ │ │ │

│ Redo Engine generates REDO │ │ RFS Process receives redo │

│ ↓ │ │ ↓ │

│ Online Redo Log (ORL) │ ─── TCP ─►│ Standby Redo Log (SRL) │

│ ↓ (LGWR/ARCn ships redo) │ │ ↓ │

│ Archive Log │ │ MRP applies redo to datafiles │

└─────────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────────┘

## 3.2 Data Guard Components

| **Component**            | **Location**       | **Role**                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary Database         | lnx107             | Production database - generates all redo                 |
| Standby Database         | lnx113             | Synchronised copy - DR target and read offload           |
| Redo Transport Services  | Primary→Standby    | Ships redo via Oracle Net (LGWR sync or ARCn async)      |
| Log Apply Services (MRP) | Standby            | Managed Recovery Process - applies redo to standby files |
| Data Guard Broker (DMON) | Both sites         | Automates management, monitoring, role transitions       |
| Observer                 | 3rd host or lnx113 | Monitors primary; triggers Fast Start Failover           |

## 3.3 Standby Database Types

| **Type**          | **Mechanism**                       | **Open Mode**                             | **Primary Use Case**             |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Physical Standby  | Redo Apply (block-level)            | MOUNTED (or READ ONLY WITH APPLY for ADG) | DR, read offload (ADG), backups  |
| Logical Standby   | SQL Apply (LogMiner)                | READ WRITE (local objects)                | Reporting, rolling upgrades      |
| Snapshot Standby  | Physical, opened R/W                | READ WRITE                                | Dev/test, patch validation       |
| Far Sync Instance | Redo forwarding only (no datafiles) | N/A - no database                         | Extended-distance zero data loss |

# 4\. Data Guard Important Terms

| **Term**                   | **Definition**                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Primary Database           | The active, read-write production database that generates all redo                               |
| Standby Database           | A synchronised copy of the primary; becomes primary on switchover/failover                       |
| DB_NAME                    | Logical database name - identical on primary and all physical standby databases                  |
| DB_UNIQUE_NAME             | Unique identifier for each Data Guard member (CDBPRIM vs CDBSTBY in this lab)                    |
| Online Redo Log (ORL)      | Circular set of logs on primary that record all changes; filled sequentially                     |
| Standby Redo Log (SRL)     | Dedicated logs on standby that receive streaming redo from primary in real-time                  |
| Archive Log                | Filled ORL archived to disk or ASM; used for transport and gap resolution                        |
| Redo Transport             | The mechanism shipping redo from primary to standby over Oracle Net                              |
| Redo Apply (MRP)           | Managed Recovery Process on physical standby - applies redo to datafiles                         |
| SQL Apply (LSP)            | LogMiner-based apply on logical standby - mines redo and executes SQL                            |
| Gap                        | Missing archived logs on standby; FAL mechanism fills gaps automatically                         |
| FAL (Fetch Archive Log)    | Gap-resolution: standby fetches missing logs from FAL_SERVER (primary)                           |
| Protection Mode            | Policy governing transport acknowledgement: Max Protection / Availability / Performance          |
| Switchover                 | Planned, graceful role reversal - both databases remain intact; zero data loss                   |
| Failover                   | Emergency promotion of standby - original primary may be unavailable; possible data loss         |
| Reinstatement              | Converting a failed primary back to standby after a failover (requires Flashback DB)             |
| Active Data Guard (ADG)    | Physical standby open READ ONLY while simultaneously applying redo (separate license)            |
| Data Guard Broker          | Management framework: DMON background process + DGMGRL command-line interface                    |
| Observer                   | Lightweight process that monitors primary and triggers Fast Start Failover automatically         |
| FSFO (Fast Start Failover) | Automatic failover to standby without DBA intervention after threshold timeout                   |
| SCAN                       | Single Client Access Name - single hostname resolving to 1-3 IPs; managed by Grid Infrastructure |
| VIP (Virtual IP)           | IP address owned by Clusterware; relocates on node failure for fast application reconnect        |
| ASM                        | Automatic Storage Management - Oracle volume manager and filesystem for database files           |
| CDB                        | Container Database - multitenant database hosting one or more Pluggable Databases (PDBs)         |
| PDB                        | Pluggable Database - portable, isolated application database inside a CDB                        |

# 5\. Data Guard Recommendations

## 5.1 Storage

- Use ASM for all database files, redo logs, and standby redo logs on both sites
- Separate +DATA (database files) and +FRA (archive logs, flashback logs, RMAN backups) into distinct disk groups
- Ensure standby storage capacity equals or exceeds primary (+DATA 80 GB, +FRA 80 GB match primary)
- Place Standby Redo Log files in +DATA or a separate disk group - never mix with archive logs in +FRA

## 5.2 Network

- Dedicate a network interface for redo transport (separate from application traffic where possible)
- Minimum 1 Gbps between primary and standby; 10 Gbps recommended for heavy OLTP
- Latency < 5 ms for synchronous (SYNC) transport - Max Availability mode; higher tolerated for ASYNC
- Open firewall port 1521 (Oracle Net) and 5500+ (DMON/Broker) between lnx107 and lnx113
- Use static listener registration (SID_LIST_LISTENER entries) for reliable Data Guard and RMAN connectivity

## 5.3 Database Parameters

- FORCE LOGGING: always ON on primary - prevents no-logging operations from creating redo gaps
- FLASHBACK DATABASE: ON on both primary and standby - enables reinstatement after failover
- STANDBY_FILE_MANAGEMENT = AUTO - automatically propagates datafile additions/drops to standby
- DG_BROKER_START = TRUE - enable broker on both nodes
- LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG with DG_CONFIG list - explicitly names all DG members

## 5.4 Standby Redo Log Sizing Rule

**NOTE:** Number of SRL groups = Number of ORL groups + 1 (per redo thread). SRL size = ORL size. In this lab: 3 ORL groups → 4 SRL groups at 200 MB each on both primary and standby.

## 5.5 Broker Best Practices

- Always use Data Guard Broker in production - never manage DG manually at scale
- Run the Observer on a third, independent host to avoid single-point-of-failure on one of the DG members
- Run VALIDATE DATABASE and VALIDATE STATIC CONNECT IDENTIFIER before enabling FSFO
- Test failover in a controlled maintenance window before relying on FSFO in production
- Set FastStartFailoverAutoReinstate = TRUE so the old primary is automatically rebuilt as standby after FSFO

# 6\. Always Configure Physical Standby First

Regardless of the ultimate goal (Active Data Guard, Snapshot Standby, Logical Standby), Oracle best practice is to always start with a physical standby. Reasons:

- Physical standby is the fastest and most reliable to create - RMAN DUPLICATE FROM ACTIVE DATABASE copies the entire primary over the network in one command
- Provides an immediately usable DR solution while additional configuration proceeds
- Can be converted to any other standby type afterwards without rebuilding
- All Oracle tools (Broker, FSFO, ADG) are physically-standby-first in design

Physical Standby (CDBSTBY)

│

├──► Active Data Guard - open READ ONLY WITH APPLY (ADG license required)

│

├──► Snapshot Standby - open READ WRITE for testing; revert discards changes

│

└──► Logical Standby - SQL Apply; local objects allowed; rolling upgrades

**TIP:** This playbook builds a Physical Standby first, then converts it to Active Data Guard. Snapshot Standby conversion is documented as a separate exercise.

| **Component**         | **Minimum**  | **lnx107 Actual**                                                                        |

## 7.2 Disk Layout per Node

| **Device** | **Size** | **Purpose**                                         | **Filesystem/Type** |
| ---------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| /dev/sda   | OS size  | Operating System                                    | XFS (LVM)           |
| /dev/sdb   | 16 GB    | Swap                                                | Linux swap          |
| /dev/sdc   | 80 GB    | +DATA ASM Disk Group (database files, spfile, redo) | Raw / ASM (udev)    |
| /dev/sdd   | 80 GB    | +FRA ASM Disk Group (archive logs, flashback, RMAN) | Raw / ASM (udev)    |
| /dev/sde   | 60 GB    | /u01 - Grid Home, DB Home, Oracle Inventory         | XFS                 |

**TIP:** Disk Space Assessment: The proposed layout is adequate for a lab. For production-scale testing, increase +DATA to 200 GB and +FRA to 200 GB. The /u01 (60 GB) comfortably holds the Grid home (~6 GB), DB home (~7 GB), and Inventory. RAM of 16 GB with 16 GB SWAP meets Oracle 19c Grid Infrastructure requirements (8 GB RAM minimum for full clusterware).

### 8.2.5 Configure /etc/hosts (Minimal - Loopback + Node Only)

With DNS in place, /etc/hosts should contain only the loopback entry and the node's own public hostname. Do NOT put VIP or SCAN entries in /etc/hosts when using DNS - it causes conflicts with Grid Infrastructure:

\# /etc/hosts - minimal entries only; DNS handles VIP and SCAN

127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.localdomain

::1 localhost6 localhost6.localdomain6

192.168.1.107 lnx107.home.aarisha.com lnx107

10.10.10.104 lnx107-priv.home.aarisha.com lnx107-priv

\# DO NOT add VIP or SCAN entries - DNS manages them

**ℹ DNS vs /etc/hosts for SCAN**

Oracle documentation requires SCAN to be resolvable via DNS (not /etc/hosts) when using Oracle 11gR2 and later. The Grid installer validates SCAN resolution through DNS specifically. If SCAN is in /etc/hosts only, the installer may issue a warning or fail prerequisite checks.

\[root@lnx107 ~\]# cat /etc/hosts

127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.localdomain localhost4 localhost4.localdomain4

::1 localhost localhost.localdomain localhost6 localhost6.localdomain6

**\# Node public IP - must match ORACLE_HOSTNAME in response file**

192.168.1.107 lnx107.home.aarisha.com lnx107

**\# Private interconnect**

10.10.10.104 lnx107-priv.home.aarisha.com lnx107-priv

### 8.2.8 E1000 on the private interconnect

**E1000 on the private interconnect is actually beneficial for Oracle Grid** because:

- E1000 emulates a real Intel NIC with full socket option support
- VirtIO's virtual NIC sometimes has limitations with low-level socket operations that Oracle's GIPCD uses for TLS handshaking

Set ens19 to use Inetl E1000.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Restart the VM for this change to be in effect.

### 8.2.8 Stop libvirtd and take down virbr0

The virbr0 libvirt NAT bridge causes issues because:

1. It appears as an extra network interface that CVU tries to classify
2. It can interfere with multicast socket binding

\# As Root

systemctl stop libvirtd

systemctl disable libvirtd

ip link set virbr0 down

\# Verify virbr0 is gone

ip link show | grep virbr0

\# Expected: no output or DOWN state

### 8.3.2 Make Disk Names Persistent - Proxmox Serials + udev by-id

Device names like /dev/sdb can change between reboots on Proxmox VMs. Use a two-layer approach: assign stable serial numbers in Proxmox, then use /dev/disk/by-id symlinks inside the VM.

### 8.3.3 Assign Serial Numbers in Proxmox (on Proxmox HOST as root)

**ℹ NOTE:** Run these commands on the PROXMOX HOST - not inside lnx107. Find the VMID of lnx107 first with: qm list | grep lnx107

\# On Proxmox host - replace VMID and disk paths with actual values

VMID=&lt;lnx107_vmid&gt;

\# Check current disk config

grep scsi /etc/pve/nodes/\*/qemu-server/\$VMID.conf

\# Assign serials (replace disk paths with actual values from conf)

qm set \$VMID --scsi0 &lt;os_disk_path&gt;,serial=OSDISK01

qm set \$VMID --scsi1 &lt;data_disk_path&gt;,serial=ASMDATA01

qm set \$VMID --scsi2 &lt;fra_disk_path&gt;,serial=ASMFRA01

\# Verify serials in conf

grep scsi /etc/pve/nodes/\*/qemu-server/\$VMID.conf

\# Reboot lnx107 to apply

qm reboot \$VMID

root@lnx173:~# VMID=130

root@lnx173:~# qm set \$VMID --scsi0 local2:130/vm-130-disk-0.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=OSDISK01

qm set \$VMID --scsi1 local2:130/vm-130-disk-1.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=ASMDATA01

qm set \$VMID --scsi2 local2:130/vm-130-disk-2.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=ASMFRA01

update VM 130: -scsi0 local2:130/vm-130-disk-0.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=OSDISK01

update VM 130: -scsi1 local2:130/vm-130-disk-1.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=ASMDATA01

update VM 130: -scsi2 local2:130/vm-130-disk-2.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=ASMFRA01

root@lnx173:~# grep scsi /etc/pve/nodes/\*/qemu-server/\$VMID.conf

boot: order=scsi0;ide2;net0

scsi0: local2:130/vm-130-disk-0.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=OSDISK01,size=100G

scsi1: local2:130/vm-130-disk-1.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=ASMDATA01,size=80G

scsi2: local2:130/vm-130-disk-2.qcow2,iothread=1,serial=ASMFRA01,size=80G

scsihw: virtio-scsi-single

### 8.3.4 Verify Stable by-id Paths Inside lnx107 (as root)

**ℹ NOTE:** With virtio-scsi-single, Proxmox exposes drive-scsiN identifiers that map to the scsiN slot - not boot order. These are stable even if /dev/sdX changes.

\# Show stable by-id paths - filter to QEMU SCSI disks, exclude partitions

ls -la /dev/disk/by-id/ | grep -v part | grep QEMU

\# scsi-0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi2 -> ../../sdc (80G ASM FRA)

\# scsi-SQEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_ASMDATA01 -> ../../sdb (if serial set)

\# scsi-SQEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_ASMFRA01 -> ../../sdc (if serial set)

\# Verify sizes confirm correct mapping

lsblk /dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi1

\# Expected: 80G (ASM DATA)

lsblk /dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi2

### 8.3.5 Create /dev/oracleasm/ Symlinks via udev

**🔴 CRITICAL:** Use the actual ID_SERIAL values confirmed in step 4.3.2 - they MUST match exactly. The values below are the expected lnx107 values; verify before applying.

\# Create the target directory for Oracle ASM device symlinks

mkdir -p /dev/oracleasm

\# Create udev rules file - match by serial, create stable named symlinks

cat > /etc/udev/rules.d/99-oracle-asm.rules << 'EOF'

\# Oracle ASM DATA disk (80G) - Proxmox scsi1

\# ID_SERIAL confirmed: 0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi1

KERNEL=="sd\*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}=="0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi1", OWNER="grid", GROUP="asmadmin", MODE="0660", SYMLINK+="oracleasm/DATA"

\# Oracle ASM FRA disk (80G) - Proxmox scsi2

\# ID_SERIAL confirmed: 0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi2

KERNEL=="sd\*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}=="0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi2", OWNER="grid", GROUP="asmadmin", MODE="0660", SYMLINK+="oracleasm/FRA"

EOF

\# Verify the file (must be single lines, no backslash continuations)

cat /etc/udev/rules.d/99-oracle-asm.rules

\# Apply rules immediately

udevadm control --reload-rules

udevadm trigger --action=add --subsystem-match=block

\# CRITICAL: verify block device ownership

ls -la /dev/sdb /dev/sdc

\# Expected: brw-rw---- 1 grid asmadmin ... /dev/sdb

\# brw-rw---- 1 grid asmadmin ... /dev/sdc

\# Verify symlinks exist

ls -la /dev/oracleasm/

\# Expected: DATA -> ../sdb FRA -> ../sdc

\# Confirm grid user can read both devices

su - grid -c "dd if=/dev/oracleasm/DATA of=/dev/null bs=512 count=1 2>&1"

su - grid -c "dd if=/dev/oracleasm/FRA of=/dev/null bs=512 count=1 2>&1"

\# Both expected: 1+0 records in / 1+0 records out

\# Reboot and verify ownership and symlinks survive

reboot

\# After reboot:

ls -la /dev/sdb /dev/sdc # must show grid:asmadmin 0660

ls -la /dev/oracleasm/ # must show DATA and FRA symlinks

\[root@lnx107 ~\]# mkdir -p /dev/oracleasm

\[root@lnx107 ~\]# cat > /etc/udev/rules.d/99-oracle-asm.rules << 'EOF'

\> **\# Oracle ASM DATA disk (80G) - Proxmox scsi1**

\> **\# ID_SERIAL confirmed: 0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi1**

\> KERNEL=="sd\*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}=="0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi1", OWNER="grid", GROUP="asmadmin", MODE="0660", SYMLINK+="oracleasm/DATA"

\>

\> **\# Oracle ASM FRA disk (80G) - Proxmox scsi2**

\> EOF

## 8.4 Provision /dev/sdc as the +FRA ASM Disk Group

**ℹ NOTE:** +FRA is created manually after Grid is running (Step 7.1). The udev rule above already covers /dev/sdc with the correct ownership.

| **Component**                     | **Size** | **Rationale**                                              |
| --------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| CDB + PDB1 + PDB2 datafiles       | ~15 GB   | System, SYSAUX, USERS, UNDO, TEMP per PDB × 2              |
| Archivelog retention (Data Guard) | ~30 GB   | 2× DB size - held until standby confirms receipt           |
| Flashback Database logs           | ~10 GB   | 60-min retention for primary reinstatement after failover  |
| RMAN backup space                 | ~20 GB   | Optional - if backing up to FRA before shipping to standby |
| Headroom / growth buffer          | ~5 GB    | Prevent ORA-19809 space exhaustion errors                  |
| Recommended /dev/sdc size         | 80 GB    | Comfortable for a lab/home DG environment with 2 PDBs      |

### 8.5.3. Passwordless SSH Configuration

Oracle Grid Infrastructure requires passwordless SSH between both nodes for both the grid and oracle users. Run these steps on BOTH nodes.

\# ─── As grid user ───────────────────────

su - grid

ssh-keygen -t rsa -N '' -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa

ssh-keygen -t dsa -N '' -f ~/.ssh/id_dsa

exit

\# ─── As oracle user ─────────────────────

su - oracle

ssh-keygen -t rsa -N '' -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa

ssh-keygen -t dsa -N '' -f ~/.ssh/id_dsa

exit

### 8.5.4 Exchange SSH Keys

**\# --- As grid user --------------------------------**

su - grid

cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

cat ~/.ssh/id_dsa.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

chmod 700 ~/.ssh

chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

exit

**\# --- As oracle user --------------------------------**

su - oracle

cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

cat ~/.ssh/id_dsa.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

chmod 700 ~/.ssh

chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

exit

## 8.7 Grid Infrastructure Silent Installation

### 8.6.1 Create Grid Response File

The cluster name bug causes CLSRSC-119 - try shortening the cluster name to under 15 characters. Change the response file to have the cluster name under 15 characters.

\# As grid user on lnx107

su - grid

cat > /u01/shared/software/response/lnx107_grid_install.rsp << 'EOF'

###############################################################################

\## Oracle Grid Infrastructure 19c - Silent Install Response File ##

\## Architecture: Single Node Full Clusterware (CRS_CONFIG + STANDALONE) ##

\## Storage: FLEX_ASM_STORAGE - OCR/voting in ASM +DATA disk group ##

\## Verified pattern: identical to lnx103 successful install ##

###############################################################################

oracle.install.responseFileVersion=/oracle/install/rspfmt_crsinstall_response_schema_v19.0.0

\# -- SECTION A - BASIC ----------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.option=CRS_CONFIG

ORACLE_BASE=/u01/app/grid

ORACLE_HOME=/u01/app/19.0.0/grid

INVENTORY_LOCATION=/u01/app/oraInventory

ORACLE_HOSTNAME=lnx107.home.aarisha.com

SELECTED_LANGUAGES=en

\# -- SECTION B - GROUPS --------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.asm.OSDBA=asmdba

oracle.install.asm.OSOPER=asmoper

oracle.install.asm.OSASM=asmadmin

\# -- SECTION C - SCAN ----------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.crs.config.scanType=LOCAL_SCAN

oracle.install.crs.config.gpnp.scanName=lnx107-scan.home.aarisha.com

oracle.install.crs.config.gpnp.scanPort=1521

\# -- SECTION D - CLUSTER -------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.crs.config.ClusterConfiguration=STANDALONE

oracle.install.crs.config.configureAsExtendedCluster=false

oracle.install.crs.config.clusterName=lnx107cluster

oracle.install.crs.config.gpnp.configureGNS=false

oracle.install.crs.config.autoConfigureClusterNodeVIP=false

oracle.install.crs.config.clusterNodes=lnx107.home.aarisha.com:lnx107-vip.home.aarisha.com

\# -- SECTION E - NETWORK -------------------------------------------------

\# ens18=Public(1), ens19=ASM & Private(5), virbr0=Do Not Use(3)

\# virbr0 MUST be listed with role 3 - CVU fails if libvirt bridge is excluded

oracle.install.crs.config.networkInterfaceList=ens18:192.168.1.0:1,ens19:10.10.10.0:5

\# -- SECTION F - STORAGE -------------------------------------------------

\# FLEX_ASM_STORAGE: OCR and voting disk stored inside the ASM DATA disk group

oracle.install.crs.config.storageOption=FLEX_ASM_STORAGE

oracle.install.crs.configureGIMR=false

oracle.install.asm.configureGIMRDataDG=false

\# -- SECTION G - ASM DISK GROUP ------------------------------------------

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.redundancy=EXTERNAL

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.AUSize=4

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.diskDiscoveryString=/dev/oracleasm/\*

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.disks=/dev/oracleasm/DATA

oracle.install.asm.configureAFD=false

\# -- PASSWORDS ------------------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.asm.SYSASMPassword=Ishan123#

oracle.install.asm.monitorPassword=Ishan123#

\# -- ENTERPRISE MANAGER & AUTO UPDATES ------------------------------------

oracle.install.config.managementOption=NONE

oracle.installer.autoupdates.option=SKIP_UPDATES

EOF

chown grid:oinstall /u01/shared/software/response/lnx107_grid_install.rsp

chmod 640 /u01/shared/software/response/lnx107_grid_install.rsp

## 8.7 Create +DATA and +FRA ASM Disk Groups

After Grid Infrastructure installation, the OCR disk group was created on /dev/sdc. Create separate +DATA and +FRA disk groups. In this lab, /dev/sdc is used for +DATA (OCR is placed in +DATA), and /dev/sdd for +FRA.

\# As grid user - connect to ASM instance

su - grid

sqlplus / as sysasm

\-- Check existing disk groups

SELECT name, state, type, total_mb, free_mb FROM v\$asm_diskgroup;

\-- Create +FRA disk group on /dev/sdd

CREATE DISKGROUP FRA EXTERNAL REDUNDANCY DISK '/dev/oracleasm/FRA' ATTRIBUTE 'compatible.asm' = '19.0';

\-- Verify

SELECT name, state, type, total_mb, free_mb FROM v\$asm_diskgroup;

EXIT;

\# Rename OCR/initial disk group to DATA if needed:

\# If the installer named it OCR, you can rename via:

\# ALTER DISKGROUP OCR RENAME TO DATA;

\# Or create a fresh +DATA group and move the OCR location - advanced step.

\# Simplest lab approach: let Grid use +DATA for both OCR and database files.

In an Oracle Data Guard configuration, you add **Standby Redo Logs (SRLs)** to the primary database to **ensure a seamless role transition during a switchover or failover.**

While SRLs are actively used only when a database operates in the **standby** role, Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture (MAA) best practices mandate creating them on both sides for the following strategic reasons:

**1\. Instant Protection After Role Reversal**

When you perform a planned switchover or an unplanned failover, your primary database becomes the new standby database. If the original primary does not already have SRLs configured, the new standby will be **unable to receive redo data in real time**. It would be forced to wait for an entire online redo log to fill up, switch, and archive on the new primary before it can be shipped. Pre-creating them ensures the new standby functions optimally with zero administrative lag.

**2\. Enables "Real-Time Apply" Post-Switchover**

Real-Time Apply allows a standby database to apply changes immediately as they are written to the SRLs, rather than waiting for an archived log file. By adding SRLs to the primary now, you guarantee that once it flips to a standby role, it can **immediately use Real-Time Apply** to maintain a near-zero Recovery Time Objective (RTO).

**3\. Preserves Maximum Protection / Maximum Availability Modes**

If your Data Guard environment uses **Maximum Protection** or **Maximum Availability** modes, SRLs are strictly mandatory. If you switch over to a primary that lacks SRLs, the Data Guard broker or configuration will fail to maintain these strict security modes. The primary database could even safely shut down or lower its protection level to Maximum Performance because it cannot find the target SRLs to guarantee zero data loss.

**4\. Configuration Symmetry and Automation**

Creating identical SRL structures on both the primary and standby databases ensures environment symmetry. It allows automation tools, like Oracle Data Guard Broker, to seamlessly validate, check, and manage the environment without failing validation rules during health checks.

# 9\. Data Guard Architecture

## 9.1 Redo Transport Architecture

PRIMARY (lnx107) STANDBY (lnx113)

───────────────── ────────────────

Application DML/DDL

│

▼

Oracle Redo Engine

│

▼

Online Redo Log (ORL) ──── Oracle Net ────► RFS Process

(LGWR writes / ships) TCP 1521 (receives redo)

│ │

│ ▼

▼ Standby Redo Log (SRL)

Archive Log ◄── log switch │

(also shipped if gap) ▼

MRP (Managed Recovery)

(applies redo to datafiles)

│

▼

Physical Standby Datafiles

(block-for-block identical)

## 9.2 Background Processes

| **Process** | **Location** | **Role**                                                                           |
| ----------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| LGWR        | Primary      | Writes to ORL; in SYNC mode sends redo to standby and waits for ACK                |
| ARCn        | Primary      | Archives filled ORL; ships in ASYNC mode; fills gaps via FAL                       |
| RFS         | Standby      | Remote File Server - receives redo from primary; writes to SRL                     |
| MRP0        | Standby      | Managed Recovery Process - applies SRL/archived logs to datafiles; real-time apply |
| DMON        | Both         | Data Guard Monitor - Broker background process; manages config/transitions         |
| NSV         | Both         | Network Server - Broker inter-node communication                                   |
| RSM         | Both         | Role Manager - coordinates switchover and failover operations                      |

## 9.3 SCAN and VIP in the Data Guard Context

Each site runs single-node Grid Infrastructure with SCAN and VIP. From a Data Guard transport perspective, redo flows between the primary and standby using their SCAN listeners or dedicated TNS aliases. After a switchover, the VIP on the new primary's site becomes active, and application connections can be routed to the new SCAN listener.

CLIENT CONNECTIONS

│

▼

lnx107-scan.home.aarisha.com:1521 (SCAN Listener - Primary Site)

│

└──► lnx107 VIP (192.168.1.108)

│

└──► CDBPRIM Instance (PRIMARY)

│

│ Redo Transport (LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2)

└──────────────────────────────────────►

CDBSTBY (lnx113)

Via: lnx113-scan or direct lnx113

RFS → MRP → Physical Datafiles

## 10.2 DNS - Verify Name Resolution

All hostnames must resolve correctly before Grid Infrastructure installation. Oracle's CVU (Cluster Verification Utility) will fail if DNS is not correct.

### 10.2.1 Network Layout

| **Bridge** | **Purpose**                             | **Guest NIC** | **IP**            |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------- |
| vmbr0      | Public network (management + client)    | ens18         | 192.1610.1.107/24 |
| vmbr1      | Private interconnect (Clusterware)      | ens19         | 10.10.10.105/24   |
| virbr0     | libvirt NAT bridge - Do Not Use in Grid | (host bridge) | 192.1610.122.1/24 |

### 10.2.2 lnx113 IP Assignment

| **Role**             | **Hostname (FQDN)**          | **IP Address** | **Interface**        |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------- |
| Public (Node)        | lnx113.home.aarisha.com      | 192.168.1.113  | ens18 / vmbr0        |
| Private Interconnect | lnx113-priv.home.aarisha.com | 10.10.10.105   | ens19 / vmbr1        |
| Virtual IP (VIP)     | lnx113-vip.home.aarisha.com  | 192.168.1.114  | ens18 (Grid-managed) |
| SCAN                 | lnx113-scan.home.aarisha.com | 192.168.1.115  | ens18 (Grid-managed) |
| DNS Server           | ns1.home.aarisha.com         | 192.168.1.111  | existing             |

**⚠ WARNING:** VIP 192.168.1.114 and SCAN 192.168.1.115 must NOT be pingable before Grid installation. Oracle Clusterware takes ownership. Confirm: ping -c 2 192.168.1.114 and ping -c 2 192.168.1.115 - both must show 100% packet loss.

### 10.2.5 Configure /etc/hosts (Minimal - Loopback + Node Only)

With DNS in place, /etc/hosts should contain only the loopback entry and the node's own public hostname. Do NOT put VIP or SCAN entries in /etc/hosts when using DNS - it causes conflicts with Grid Infrastructure:

\# /etc/hosts - minimal entries only; DNS handles VIP and SCAN

127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.localdomain

::1 localhost6 localhost6.localdomain6

192.168.1.113 lnx113.home.aarisha.com lnx113

10.10.10.105 lnx113-priv.home.aarisha.com lnx113-priv

\# DO NOT add VIP or SCAN entries - DNS manages them

**ℹ DNS vs /etc/hosts for SCAN**

Oracle documentation requires SCAN to be resolvable via DNS (not /etc/hosts) when using Oracle 11gR2 and later. The Grid installer validates SCAN resolution through DNS specifically. If SCAN is in /etc/hosts only, the installer may issue a warning or fail prerequisite checks.

\[root@lnx113 ~\]# cat /etc/hosts

127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.localdomain localhost4 localhost4.localdomain4

::1 localhost localhost.localdomain localhost6 localhost6.localdomain6

**\# Node public IP - must match ORACLE_HOSTNAME in response file**

192.168.1.113 lnx113.home.aarisha.com lnx113

**\# Private interconnect**

10.10.10.105 lnx113-priv.home.aarisha.com lnx113-priv

### 10.2.8 E1000 on the private interconnect

**E1000 on the private interconnect is actually beneficial for Oracle Grid** because:

- E1000 emulates a real Intel NIC with full socket option support
- VirtIO's virtual NIC sometimes has limitations with low-level socket operations that Oracle's GIPCD uses for TLS handshaking

Set ens19 to use Inetl E1000.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Restart the VM for this change to be in effect.

### 10.2.8 Stop libvirtd and take down virbr0

The virbr0 libvirt NAT bridge causes issues because:

1. It appears as an extra network interface that CVU tries to classify
2. It can interfere with multicast socket binding

systemctl disable libvirtd

ip link set virbr0 down

### 10.2.9 Disable IPV6

The GI installer detects IPv6 addresses on NICs and may fail or generate confusing errors. Disable IPv6 on both nodes before running the installer.

net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6 = 1

net.ipv6.conf.ens18.disable_ipv6 = 1

net.ipv6.conf.ens19.disable_ipv6 = 1

EOF

ip addr show ens18 | grep inet6 # must return nothing

ip addr show ens19 | grep inet6 # must return nothing

### 10.2.10 Disable Firewall

**Firewalld was blocking multicast** - that's the root cause on lnx113. The firewall was dropping the multicast UDP packets that CVU uses for its loopback test.

Add this to the pre-installation checklist for all future nodes:

\# ─── Run as root ──────────────────────────────

\# Stop and disable firewalld before Grid installation

systemctl stop firewalld

systemctl disable firewalld

### 10.3.2 Make Disk Names Persistent - Proxmox Serials + udev by-id

Device names like /dev/sdb can change between reboots on Proxmox VMs. Use a two-layer approach: assign stable serial numbers in Proxmox, then use /dev/disk/by-id symlinks inside the VM.

### 10.3.3 Assign Serial Numbers in Proxmox (on Proxmox HOST as root)

**ℹ NOTE:** Run these commands on the PROXMOX HOST - not inside lnx113. Find the VMID of lnx113 first with: qm list | grep lnx113

\# On Proxmox host - replace VMID and disk paths with actual values

VMID=&lt;lnx113_vmid&gt;

\# Check current disk config

grep scsi /etc/pve/nodes/\*/qemu-server/\$VMID.conf

\# Assign serials (replace disk paths with actual values from conf)

qm set \$VMID --scsi0 &lt;os_disk_path&gt;,serial=OSDISK01

qm set \$VMID --scsi1 &lt;data_disk_path&gt;,serial=ASMDATA01

qm set \$VMID --scsi2 &lt;fra_disk_path&gt;,serial=ASMFRA01

\# Verify serials in conf

grep scsi /etc/pve/nodes/\*/qemu-server/\$VMID.conf

\# Reboot lnx113 to apply

qm reboot \$VMID

### 10.3.5 Create /dev/oracleasm/ Symlinks via udev

**🔴 CRITICAL:** Use the actual ID_SERIAL values confirmed in step 4.3.2 - they MUST match exactly. The values below are the expected lnx113 values; verify before applying.

\# Create the target directory for Oracle ASM device symlinks

mkdir -p /dev/oracleasm

\# Create udev rules file - match by serial, create stable named symlinks

cat > /etc/udev/rules.d/99-oracle-asm.rules << 'EOF'

\# Oracle ASM DATA disk (80G) - Proxmox scsi1

\# ID_SERIAL confirmed: 0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi1

KERNEL=="sd\*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}=="0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi1", OWNER="grid", GROUP="asmadmin", MODE="0660", SYMLINK+="oracleasm/DATA"

\# Oracle ASM FRA disk (80G) - Proxmox scsi2

\# ID_SERIAL confirmed: 0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi2

KERNEL=="sd\*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}=="0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi2", OWNER="grid", GROUP="asmadmin", MODE="0660", SYMLINK+="oracleasm/FRA"

EOF

\# Verify the file (must be single lines, no backslash continuations)

cat /etc/udev/rules.d/99-oracle-asm.rules

\# Apply rules immediately

udevadm control --reload-rules

udevadm trigger --action=add --subsystem-match=block

\# CRITICAL: verify block device ownership

ls -la /dev/sdb /dev/sdc

\# Expected: brw-rw---- 1 grid asmadmin ... /dev/sdb

\# brw-rw---- 1 grid asmadmin ... /dev/sdc

\# Verify symlinks exist

ls -la /dev/oracleasm/

\# Expected: DATA -> ../sdb FRA -> ../sdc

su - grid -c "dd if=/dev/oracleasm/FRA of=/dev/null bs=512 count=1 2>&1"

reboot

ls -la /dev/oracleasm/ # must show DATA and FRA symlinks

## 10.4 Provision /dev/sdc as the +FRA ASM Disk Group

**ℹ NOTE:** +FRA is created manually after Grid is running (Step 7.1). The udev rule above already covers /dev/sdc with the correct ownership.

| **Component**                     | **Size** | **Rationale**                                              |
| --------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| CDB + PDB1 + PDB2 datafiles       | ~15 GB   | System, SYSAUX, USERS, UNDO, TEMP per PDB × 2              |
| Archivelog retention (Data Guard) | ~30 GB   | 2× DB size - held until standby confirms receipt           |
| Flashback Database logs           | ~10 GB   | 60-min retention for primary reinstatement after failover  |
| RMAN backup space                 | ~20 GB   | Optional - if backing up to FRA before shipping to standby |
| Headroom / growth buffer          | ~5 GB    | Prevent ORA-19809 space exhaustion errors                  |
| Recommended /dev/sdc size         | 80 GB    | Comfortable for a lab/home DG environment with 2 PDBs      |

### 10.5.3. Passwordless SSH Configuration

Oracle Grid Infrastructure requires passwordless SSH between both nodes for both the grid and oracle users. Run these steps on BOTH nodes.

\# ─── As grid user ───────────────────────

su - grid

ssh-keygen -t rsa -N '' -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa

ssh-keygen -t dsa -N '' -f ~/.ssh/id_dsa

exit

\# ─── As oracle user ─────────────────────

su - oracle

ssh-keygen -t rsa -N '' -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa

ssh-keygen -t dsa -N '' -f ~/.ssh/id_dsa

exit

### 10.5.4 Exchange SSH Keys

**\# --- As grid user --------------------------------**

su - grid

cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

cat ~/.ssh/id_dsa.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

chmod 700 ~/.ssh

chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

exit

**\# --- As oracle user --------------------------------**

su - oracle

cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

cat ~/.ssh/id_dsa.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

chmod 700 ~/.ssh

chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

exit

**\# --- As grid user --------------------------------**

su - grid

ssh-keyscan -H lnx113 >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

ssh-keyscan -H lnx113.home.aarisha.com >> ~/.ssh/known_host

exit

**\# --- As oracle --------------------------------**

su - oracle

ssh-keyscan -H lnx113 >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

ssh-keyscan -H lnx113.home.aarisha.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

exit

## 10.7 Grid Infrastructure Silent Installation

### 10.7.1 Create Grid Response File

The cluster name bug causes CLSRSC-119 - try shortening the cluster name to under 15 characters. Change the response file to have the cluster name under 15 characters.

\# As grid user on lnx113

su - grid

cat > /u01/shared/software/response/lnx113_grid_install.rsp << 'EOF'

###############################################################################

\## Oracle Grid Infrastructure 19c - Silent Install Response File ##

\## Architecture: Single Node Full Clusterware (CRS_CONFIG + STANDALONE) ##

\## Storage: FLEX_ASM_STORAGE - OCR/voting in ASM +DATA disk group ##

\## Verified pattern: identical to lnx103 successful install ##

###############################################################################

oracle.install.responseFileVersion=/oracle/install/rspfmt_crsinstall_response_schema_v19.0.0

\# -- SECTION A - BASIC ----------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.option=CRS_CONFIG

ORACLE_BASE=/u01/app/grid

ORACLE_HOME=/u01/app/19.0.0/grid

INVENTORY_LOCATION=/u01/app/oraInventory

ORACLE_HOSTNAME=lnx113.home.aarisha.com

SELECTED_LANGUAGES=en

\# -- SECTION B - GROUPS --------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.asm.OSDBA=asmdba

oracle.install.asm.OSOPER=asmoper

oracle.install.asm.OSASM=asmadmin

\# -- SECTION C - SCAN ----------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.crs.config.scanType=LOCAL_SCAN

oracle.install.crs.config.gpnp.scanName=lnx113-scan.home.aarisha.com

oracle.install.crs.config.gpnp.scanPort=1521

\# -- SECTION D - CLUSTER -------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.crs.config.ClusterConfiguration=STANDALONE

oracle.install.crs.config.configureAsExtendedCluster=false

oracle.install.crs.config.clusterName=lnx113cluster

oracle.install.crs.config.gpnp.configureGNS=false

oracle.install.crs.config.autoConfigureClusterNodeVIP=false

oracle.install.crs.config.clusterNodes=lnx113.home.aarisha.com:lnx113-vip.home.aarisha.com

\# -- SECTION E - NETWORK -------------------------------------------------

\# ens18=Public(1), ens19=ASM & Private(5), virbr0=Do Not Use(3)

\# virbr0 MUST be listed with role 3 - CVU fails if libvirt bridge is excluded

oracle.install.crs.config.networkInterfaceList=ens18:192.1610.1.0:1,ens19:10.10.10.0:5

\# -- SECTION F - STORAGE -------------------------------------------------

\# FLEX_ASM_STORAGE: OCR and voting disk stored inside the ASM DATA disk group

oracle.install.crs.config.storageOption=FLEX_ASM_STORAGE

oracle.install.crs.configureGIMR=false

oracle.install.asm.configureGIMRDataDG=false

\# -- SECTION G - ASM DISK GROUP ------------------------------------------

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.name=DATA

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.redundancy=EXTERNAL

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.AUSize=4

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.diskDiscoveryString=/dev/oracleasm/\*

oracle.install.asm.diskGroup.disks=/dev/oracleasm/DATA

oracle.install.asm.configureAFD=false

\# -- PASSWORDS ------------------------------------------------------------

oracle.install.asm.SYSASMPassword=Ishan123#

oracle.install.asm.monitorPassword=Ishan123#

\# -- ENTERPRISE MANAGER & AUTO UPDATES ------------------------------------

oracle.install.config.managementOption=NONE

oracle.installer.autoupdates.option=SKIP_UPDATES

EOF

chown grid:oinstall /u01/shared/software/response/lnx113_grid_install.rsp

chmod 640 /u01/shared/software/response/lnx113_grid_install.rsp

## 10.8 Create +DATA and +FRA ASM Disk Groups

After Grid Infrastructure installation, the OCR disk group was created on /dev/sdc. Create separate +DATA and +FRA disk groups. In this lab, /dev/sdc is used for +DATA (OCR is placed in +DATA), and /dev/sdd for +FRA.

\# As grid user - connect to ASM instance

su - grid

sqlplus / as sysasm

\-- Check existing disk groups

SELECT name, state, type, total_mb, free_mb FROM v\$asm_diskgroup;

\-- Create +FRA disk group on /dev/sdd

CREATE DISKGROUP FRA EXTERNAL REDUNDANCY DISK '/dev/oracleasm/FRA' ATTRIBUTE 'compatible.asm' = '19.0';

\-- Verify

SELECT name, state, type, total_mb, free_mb FROM v\$asm_diskgroup;

EXIT;

\# Rename OCR/initial disk group to DATA if needed:

\# If the installer named it OCR, you can rename via:

\# ALTER DISKGROUP OCR RENAME TO DATA;

\# Or create a fresh +DATA group and move the OCR location - advanced step.

\# Simplest lab approach: let Grid use +DATA for both OCR and database files.

## 10.10 Password less SSH Login for user oracle and grid on both hosts lnx107 and lnx113

For Data Guard setup you need passwordless SSH in **both directions** and for **both oracle and grid users**. Here is why:

Who Needs Passwordless SSH

| **User** | **Direction**   | **Why**                                 |
| -------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| oracle   | lnx107 → lnx113 | scp password file, RMAN DUPLICATE       |
| oracle   | lnx113 → lnx107 | RMAN DUPLICATE can run from either node |
| grid     | lnx107 → lnx113 | Clusterware management, srvctl          |
| grid     | lnx113 → lnx107 | Clusterware management, srvctl          |

On lnx107 (as oracle)

su - oracle

ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub oracle@lnx113

\# Test

ssh oracle@lnx113 "hostname"

ssh <oracle@lnx113.home.aarisha.com> "hostname"

On lnx113 (as oracle)

su - oracle

ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub oracle@lnx107

\# Test

ssh oracle@lnx107 "hostname"

ssh <oracle@lnx107.home.aarisha.com> "hostname"

On lnx107 (as grid)

\# Test

# 12\. Primary Database Changes for Data Guard

These parameter changes configure the primary database to ship redo to CDBSTBY and enable Data Guard Broker.

\-- Connect to primary as SYSDBA

sqlplus / as sysdba

\-- LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_1: local archive to +FRA

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_1=

'LOCATION=+FRA VALID_FOR=(ALL_LOGFILES,ALL_ROLES) DB_UNIQUE_NAME=CDBPRIM'

SCOPE=BOTH;

\-- LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2: transport to standby (ASYNC for initial setup)

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2=

'SERVICE=CDBSTBY ASYNC VALID_FOR=(ONLINE_LOGFILES,PRIMARY_ROLE) DB_UNIQUE_NAME=CDBSTBY'

SCOPE=BOTH;

\-- Enable destination 2

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_STATE_2 = ENABLE SCOPE=BOTH;

\-- FAL: gap resolution

ALTER SYSTEM SET FAL_SERVER = 'CDBSTBY' SCOPE=BOTH;

ALTER SYSTEM SET FAL_CLIENT = 'CDBPRIM' SCOPE=BOTH;

\-- Standby file management: auto propagate datafile changes

ALTER SYSTEM SET STANDBY_FILE_MANAGEMENT = AUTO SCOPE=BOTH;

\-- Enable Data Guard Broker

ALTER SYSTEM SET DG_BROKER_START = TRUE SCOPE=BOTH;

\-- Log archive config: list all DG members

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG =

'DG_CONFIG=(CDBPRIM,CDBSTBY)'

SCOPE=BOTH;

\-- Remote login password file: required for DG redo transport authentication

ALTER SYSTEM SET REMOTE_LOGIN_PASSWORDFILE = EXCLUSIVE SCOPE=SPFILE;

\-- DB_UNIQUE_NAME (verify - set during database creation)

SHOW PARAMETER DB_UNIQUE_NAME;

\-- Expected: CDBPRIM

\-- Bounce the database to pick up SPFILE changes

SHUTDOWN IMMEDIATE;

STARTUP;

\-- Enable Flashback Database (if not already on)

ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK ON;

\-- Verify all parameters

SELECT NAME, VALUE FROM V\$PARAMETER

WHERE NAME IN (

'db_unique_name','log_archive_dest_1','log_archive_dest_2',

'log_archive_dest_state_2','log_archive_config',

'fal_server','fal_client','standby_file_management',

'dg_broker_start','remote_login_passwordfile'

);

## 12.1 Add Static Listener to GRID's \$ORACLE_HOME

The listener is using the **Grid home's listener.ora** (/u01/app/19.0.0/grid/network/admin/listener.ora), not the DB home's listener.ora. The static CDBPRIM entries were added to the wrong file in chapter 11.

The Grid-managed listener reads from /u01/app/19.0.0/grid/network/admin/listener.ora - not \$ORACLE_HOME/network/admin/listener.ora.

Also notice CDBPRIM is not showing - the database dynamic registration hasn't happened yet either. Fix both:

\# On lnx107 as root

\# As root - edit the Grid listener.ora

cat >> /u01/app/19.0.0/grid/network/admin/listener.ora << 'EOF'

SID_LIST_LISTENER =

(SID_LIST =

(SID_DESC =

(GLOBAL_DBNAME = CDBPRIM)

(ORACLE_HOME = /u01/app/oracle/product/19.0.0/dbhome_1)

(SID_NAME = CDBPRIM)

)

(SID_DESC =

(GLOBAL_DBNAME = CDBPRIM_DGMGRL)

(ORACLE_HOME = /u01/app/oracle/product/19.0.0/dbhome_1)

(SID_NAME = CDBPRIM)

)

)

EOF

cat /u01/app/19.0.0/grid/network/admin/listener.ora

## 13.3 RMAN DUPLICATE FROM ACTIVE DATABASE

Run RMAN on lnx107 (primary) or lnx113 (standby). RMAN connects to the primary as TARGET and the standby auxiliary instance as AUXILIARY.

\# On lnx107 (or lnx113) as oracle

rman target sys/ishan123@CDBPRIM_DIRECT auxiliary sys/ishan123@CDBSTBY_DIRECT

DUPLICATE TARGET DATABASE

FOR STANDBY

FROM ACTIVE DATABASE

DORECOVER

SPFILE

PARAMETER_VALUE_CONVERT 'CDBPRIM','CDBSTBY'

SET DB_NAME='CDBPRIM'

SET DB_UNIQUE_NAME='CDBSTBY'

SET DB_FILE_NAME_CONVERT='+DATA/CDBPRIM','+DATA/CDBSTBY'

SET LOG_FILE_NAME_CONVERT='+DATA/CDBPRIM','+DATA/CDBSTBY'

SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_1='LOCATION=+FRA VALID_FOR=(ALL_LOGFILES,ALL_ROLES) DB_UNIQUE_NAME=CDBSTBY'

SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2='SERVICE=CDBPRIM ASYNC VALID_FOR=(ONLINE_LOGFILES,PRIMARY_ROLE) DB_UNIQUE_NAME=CDBPRIM'

SET FAL_SERVER='CDBPRIM'

SET FAL_CLIENT='CDBSTBY'

SET STANDBY_FILE_MANAGEMENT='AUTO'

SET DG_BROKER_START='TRUE'

SET LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG='DG_CONFIG=(CDBPRIM,CDBSTBY)'

NOFILENAMECHECK;

**TIP:** RMAN DUPLICATE copies all datafiles over Oracle Net. For a database sized at several GB this takes 15-45 minutes. Watch progress via: tail -f /u01/app/oracle/diag/rdbms/cdbstby/CDBSTBY/trace/alert_CDBSTBY.log

### 13.4.1 Add SRLs on Primary (lnx107) - No MRP Running

\-- As oracle on lnx107

sqlplus / as sysdba

\-- Check existing ORL count

SELECT COUNT(\*) FROM V\$LOG;

\-- Expected: 3

\-- Add SRL groups 4-7 (minimum - ORL+1)

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 4 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 5 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 6 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 7 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

\-- Add groups 8-10 for symmetry with standby (future role)

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 8 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 9 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 10 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

\-- Verify - 7 groups total

SELECT GROUP#, BYTES/1024/1024 AS SIZE_MB, STATUS

FROM V\$STANDBY_LOG ORDER BY GROUP#;

\-- Expected: Groups 4-10, all 200MB, UNASSIGNED

### 13.4.2 Add SRLs on Standby (lnx113) - Cancel MRP First

\-- As oracle on lnx113

sqlplus / as sysdba

\-- Step 1: Cancel MRP before adding SRLs

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE CANCEL;

\-- Step 2: Add SRL groups 4-10 (symmetric with primary)

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 4 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 5 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 6 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 7 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 8 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 9 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 10 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

\-- Expected: Groups 4-10, all 200MB, mostly UNASSIGNED

If groups 4-10 exist with 200MB - proceed directly to starting MRP:

## 13.5 Start Managed Recovery (MRP)

\-- On standby: start real-time apply (MRP with USING CURRENT LOGFILE)

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE

USING CURRENT LOGFILE

DISCONNECT FROM SESSION;

\-- Verify MRP is running

SELECT PROCESS, STATUS, SEQUENCE# FROM V\$MANAGED_STANDBY

WHERE PROCESS = 'MRP0';

\-- Expected STATUS: APPLYING_LOG

&nbsp; USING CURRENT LOGFILE

**MRP is running!** WAIT_FOR_LOG means MRP has applied all available redo and is waiting for the next log from the primary - this is the normal healthy state.

SCAN listener on lnx113 has no CDBSTBY service registered. The SCAN listener only gets services via dynamic registration, and the standby instance in MOUNTED state doesn't register with the SCAN listener automatically.

Use CDBSTBY_DIRECT instead:

\-- On lnx107 as oracle

sqlplus / as sysdba

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2=

'SERVICE=CDBSTBY_DIRECT ASYNC VALID_FOR=(ONLINE_LOGFILES,PRIMARY_ROLE) DB_UNIQUE_NAME=CDBSTBY'

SCOPE=BOTH;

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_STATE_2=ENABLE SCOPE=BOTH;

ALTER SYSTEM SWITCH LOGFILE;

\-- Check immediately

SELECT DEST_ID, STATUS, ERROR FROM V\$ARCHIVE_DEST WHERE DEST_ID=2;

\-- On standby: start real-time apply (MRP with USING CURRENT LOGFILE)

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE

USING CURRENT LOGFILE

DISCONNECT FROM SESSION;

\-- Verify MRP is running

SELECT PROCESS, STATUS, SEQUENCE# FROM V\$MANAGED_STANDBY

WHERE PROCESS = 'MRP0';

\-- Expected STATUS: APPLYING_LOG

## 14.3 End-to-End Test

\-- On primary: create test object

\-- On lnx107 - create a test object

sqlplus / as sysdba

ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER=PDB1;

CREATE TABLE dg_test (id NUMBER, ts TIMESTAMP DEFAULT SYSTIMESTAMP);

INSERT INTO dg_test VALUES (1, SYSTIMESTAMP);

COMMIT;

\-- On lnx107

ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER=CDB\$ROOT;

ALTER SYSTEM SWITCH LOGFILE;

EXIT

\-- Wait 5-10 seconds, then on standby check apply sequence

SELECT MAX(SEQUENCE#) FROM V\$ARCHIVED_LOG WHERE APPLIED='YES';

\-- On lnx113 from CDB root

SELECT THREAD#, MAX(SEQUENCE#) AS LAST_SEQ, MAX(NEXT_CHANGE#) AS LAST_SCN

FROM V\$ARCHIVED_LOG

WHERE APPLIED='YES'

GROUP BY THREAD#;

\-- On lnx107 CDB root

SELECT CURRENT_SCN FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- Clean up on primary

DROP TABLE dg_test PURGE;

ALTER SYSTEM SWITCH LOGFILE;

If standby's LAST_SCN >= primary's CURRENT_SCN at time of insert - replication is confirmed.

Actually the simplest confirmation is already done - **MRP shows zero transport lag and zero apply lag**, which proves all redo including the PDB1 INSERT has been applied. The end-to-end test is passed.

# 15\. Configure Redo Transport

## 15.1 Transport Modes

| **Keyword** | **How it Works**                                                      | **Data Loss Risk**             | **Use Case**                                 |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| ASYNC       | LGWR does not wait for standby ACK; redo ships in background          | Possible (lag seconds-minutes) | Max Performance; WAN; minimal latency impact |
| SYNC        | LGWR waits for standby RFS to acknowledge write before commit returns | Zero (when standby available)  | Max Availability / Max Protection; LAN       |

## 15.2 Switching from ASYNC to SYNC Transport

\-- After standby is built and verified, switch to SYNC for Max Availability

\-- On lnx107 as oracle

sqlplus / as sysdba

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2=

'SERVICE=CDBSTBY_DIRECT SYNC AFFIRM

VALID_FOR=(ONLINE_LOGFILES,PRIMARY_ROLE)

DB_UNIQUE_NAME=CDBSTBY'

SCOPE=BOTH;

SHOW PARAMETER LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2;

# 16\. Data Guard Protection Modes -

DATA LOSS RISK

HIGH ◄─────────────────────────────────────────────────► NONE

Max Performance Max Availability Max Protection

(ASYNC) (SYNC + fallback) (SYNC, no fallback)

LOW ◄─────────────────────────────────────────────────► HIGH

PERFORMANCE IMPACT

| **Mode**                  | **Transport** | **ACK Required** | **Primary Halts if Standby Down?** | **Data Loss Risk**          |
| ------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Max Performance (default) | ASYNC         | No               | No                                 | Possible (seconds-minutes)  |
| Max Availability          | SYNC          | Yes              | No (falls back to ASYNC)           | Zero when standby available |
| Max Protection            | SYNC          | Yes              | YES - primary shuts down           | Zero (guaranteed)           |

**TIP:** Lab recommendation: Use Max Performance during initial setup and RMAN DUPLICATE. Switch to Max Availability once the configuration is verified stable. Max Protection is not recommended for a single-standby lab - if the standby is unavailable (e.g., for patching), the primary shuts down.

# 17\. Understanding Redo Transport

## 17.1 Real-Time Apply vs Archived Log Apply

| **Mode**                      | **MRP Command**                          | **How it Works**                          | **Lag** |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------- |
| Real-Time Apply (recommended) | USING CURRENT LOGFILE                    | MRP reads from SRL while primary writes   | Seconds |
| Archived Log Apply            | (default, without USING CURRENT LOGFILE) | MRP applies after log switch and archival | Minutes |

## 17.2 Transport Synchronization States

| **SYNCHRONIZATION_STATUS** | **Meaning**                                          |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| SYNCHRONIZED               | No transport lag - SYNC mode fully caught up         |
| APPLYING LOGS              | Logs arriving and being applied (normal ASYNC state) |
| RESYNCHRONIZING            | Gap detected; FAL is filling missing logs            |
| CHECK CONFIGURATION        | Broker parameter or connectivity issue               |

# 18\. Convert Physical Standby to Active Data Guard (ADG)

**WARNING:** Active Data Guard (READ ONLY WITH APPLY) requires the Oracle Active Data Guard license option (included in Oracle EE Extreme Performance or purchased separately).

Active Data Guard allows the physical standby to be open READ ONLY while MRP continues applying redo. This enables reporting, read offload, and backups on the standby without impacting the primary.

## 18.1 Open Standby READ ONLY WITH APPLY

\-- On standby (lnx113)

\-- Cancel current MRP

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE CANCEL;

\-- Open READ ONLY

ALTER DATABASE OPEN READ ONLY;

\-- Restart MRP (continues applying redo while database is READ ONLY)

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE

USING CURRENT LOGFILE

DISCONNECT FROM SESSION;

\-- Verify

SELECT DB_UNIQUE_NAME, DATABASE_ROLE, OPEN_MODE FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- Expected: CDBSTBY | PHYSICAL STANDBY | READ ONLY WITH APPLY

**\# lnx113 Standby**

# 19\. Data Guard Client Connection

## 19.1 Role-Based Services - Best Practice

Applications should connect via database services registered to specific roles, not directly to DB_UNIQUE_NAME. This allows connections to automatically follow role transitions after switchover/failover.

\-- On primary: create OLTP service (starts when DB is in PRIMARY role)

\# As oracle on lnx107

su - oracle

\# 1. Add PRIMARY role services to OCR (Grid registry)

srvctl add service -d CDBPRIM -s PRIMAPP \\

\-role PRIMARY -pdb PDB1

srvctl add service -d CDBPRIM -s PRIMAPP2 \\

\-role PRIMARY -pdb PDB2

\# 2. Add PHYSICAL_STANDBY role services to OCR

\# (must exist on primary even though they won't run here)

srvctl add service -d CDBPRIM -s REPORT \\

\-role PHYSICAL_STANDBY -pdb PDB1

srvctl add service -d CDBPRIM -s REPORT2 \\

\-role PHYSICAL_STANDBY -pdb PDB2

\# 3. Start PRIMARY services on primary

srvctl start service -d CDBPRIM -s PRIMAPP

srvctl start service -d CDBPRIM -s PRIMAPP2

\# 4. Create service definitions in data dictionary

\# (required for standby to start them - replicates via redo)

sqlplus / as sysdba << 'EOF'

ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER=PDB1;

BEGIN

DBMS_SERVICE.CREATE_SERVICE(

service_name => 'REPORT',

network_name => 'REPORT'

);

END;

/

ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER=PDB2;

BEGIN

DBMS_SERVICE.CREATE_SERVICE(

service_name => 'REPORT2',

network_name => 'REPORT2'

);

END;

/

ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER=CDB\$ROOT;

ALTER SYSTEM SWITCH LOGFILE;

EXIT

EOF

\# 5. Verify

srvctl status service -d CDBPRIM -s PRIMAPP

srvctl status service -d CDBPRIM -s PRIMAPP2

srvctl status service -d CDBPRIM -s REPORT

srvctl status service -d CDBPRIM -s REPORT2

\# Expected: PRIMAPP and PRIMAPP2 running, REPORT and REPORT2 not running

# 20\. Perform Manual Switchover

A switchover is a planned, graceful role reversal. Both databases remain intact and there is zero data loss. Switchover is always reversible.

## 20.1 Pre-Switchover Checklist

\-- On lnx107 as oracle

sqlplus / as sysdba

\-- 1. Verify protection mode

SELECT PROTECTION_MODE, PROTECTION_LEVEL FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- Expected: MAXIMUM AVAILABILITY

\-- 2. Verify no redo gap

SELECT \* FROM V\$ARCHIVE_GAP;

\-- Expected: no rows

\-- 3. Check transport lag

SELECT DEST_ID, STATUS, GAP_STATUS, SYNCHRONIZED

FROM V\$ARCHIVE_DEST_STATUS WHERE DEST_ID=2;

\-- On lnx113 as oracle

sqlplus / as sysdba

\-- 4. Verify MRP is running

SELECT PROCESS, STATUS, SEQUENCE#

FROM V\$MANAGED_STANDBY WHERE PROCESS='MRP0';

\-- 5. Verify zero apply lag

SELECT NAME, VALUE FROM V\$DATAGUARD_STATS

WHERE NAME IN ('transport lag','apply lag');

**Switchover complete and verified!**

| **Node** | **DB_UNIQUE_NAME** | **Role**            | **Open Mode**        |
| -------- | ------------------ | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| lnx113   | CDBSTBY            | ✅ PRIMARY          | READ WRITE           |
| lnx107   | CDBPRIM            | ✅ PHYSICAL STANDBY | READ ONLY WITH APPLY |

MRP0 is APPLYING_LOG on lnx107 - redo transport from new primary (lnx113) to new standby (lnx107) is working.

In Oracle Data Guard, **MRP0 (Managed Recovery Process)** is the critical background process responsible for applying redo data to a **physical standby database** to keep it transactionally synchronized with the primary database.

**Core Responsibilities of MRP0**

- **Redo Application**: It reads the incoming redo data directly from the Standby Redo Logs (SRLs) or Archived Redo Logs and applies those block-level changes to the physical standby database.
- **Byte-for-Byte Copy**: Because it works at the physical block level, it ensures that the standby database remains an exact, bit-for-bit replica of the primary database.
- **Gap Detection & Resolution**: If MRP0 notices a missing sequence in the archived redo logs while performing recovery, it initiates the Fetch Archive Log (FAL) request-response mechanism to fetch the missing logs from the primary server.

# 21\. Clean Shutdown - Primary and Standby

## 21.1 Shutdown Sequence

Always stop standby first, then primary:

\# STEP 1 - Stop standby MRP and shutdown (on lnx113 as oracle)

sqlplus / as sysdba << 'EOF'

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE CANCEL;

SHUTDOWN IMMEDIATE;

EXIT

EOF

\# STEP 2 - Shutdown primary (on lnx107 as oracle)

srvctl stop database -d CDBPRIM -o immediate

\# STEP 3 - Stop Grid on lnx113 (as root)

crsctl stop crs

\# STEP 4 - Stop Grid on lnx107 (as root)

crsctl stop crs

## 21.2 Startup Sequence

Always start primary first, then standby:

\# STEP 1 - Start Grid on lnx107 PRIMARY (as root)

crsctl start crs

\# Wait for CRS fully online

crsctl check crs

\# Expected: all 4 services online

\# STEP 2 - Verify primary database auto-started (as oracle on lnx107)

srvctl status database -d CDBPRIM

\# Expected: Instance CDBPRIM is running on node lnx107

\# If NOT running - start manually:

srvctl start database -d CDBPRIM

\# Verify primary is open

sqlplus / as sysdba << 'EOF'

SELECT DB_UNIQUE_NAME, DATABASE_ROLE, OPEN_MODE FROM V\$DATABASE;

SELECT CON_ID, NAME, OPEN_MODE FROM V\$PDBS ORDER BY CON_ID;

EXIT

EOF

# 22\. Perform Manual Failover

A failover is performed when the primary database is unavailable and cannot be quickly recovered. The standby is promoted to primary. Unlike switchover, failover may involve data loss (unless Max Availability mode with zero lag at the moment of failure).

## 22.4 Activate Standby as New Primary

Without deferring DEST_2, the new primary will immediately try to ship redo to the old primary (lnx107) which is down, causing ORA-12541 or ORA-01034 errors in the alert log and potentially impacting foreground transactions in MAXIMUM AVAILABILITY mode.

\-- On standby (lnx113)

\-- On lnx113 as oracle

sqlplus / as sysdba

\-- 1. DEFER DEST_2 (SCOPE=BOTH - while still standby)

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_STATE_2 = DEFER SCOPE=BOTH;

\-- Verify deferred

SELECT DEST_ID, STATUS FROM V\$ARCHIVE_DEST WHERE DEST_ID=2;

\-- Expected: INACTIVE

\-- 2. FINISH applying redo

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE FINISH FORCE;

\-- 3. ACTIVATE as primary (point of no return)

ALTER DATABASE ACTIVATE PHYSICAL STANDBY DATABASE;

\-- 4. OPEN primary

ALTER DATABASE OPEN;

\-- 5. OPEN PDBs

ALTER PLUGGABLE DATABASE ALL OPEN;

\-- 6. Start services

srvctl start service -d CDBSTBY -s PRIMAPP

srvctl start service -d CDBSTBY -s PRIMAPP2

srvctl status service -d CDBSTBY -s PRIMAPP

srvctl status service -d CDBSTBY -s PRIMAPP2

\-- Step 7: Verify role and mode

SELECT DB_UNIQUE_NAME, DATABASE_ROLE, OPEN_MODE,

PROTECTION_MODE FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- Expected: CDBSTBY | PRIMARY | READ WRITE | MAXIMUM PERFORMANCE

\-- Step 8: Confirm DEST_2 still deferred

SELECT DEST_ID, STATUS, ERROR FROM V\$ARCHIVE_DEST WHERE DEST_ID=2;

\-- Expected: INACTIVE - no errors

EXIT

\-- 7. ENABLE DEST_2 only **after lnx107 standby is rebuilt** and MRP running

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_STATE_2 = **ENABLE** SCOPE=BOTH;

Why SCOPE=BOTH (not SCOPE=SPFILE)

| **Scope**    | **When to Use**                                              | **Why**                                                                         |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SCOPE=BOTH   | **Before activation** - instance is still running as standby | Changes memory AND spfile - takes effect immediately AND persists after restart |
| SCOPE=SPFILE | After activation if instance needs restart                   | Only changes spfile - does NOT take effect until next startup                   |
| SCOPE=MEMORY | Temporary change only - won't survive restart                | Changes memory only - lost after restart                                        |

The correct choice is **SCOPE=BOTH before activation** because:

- The instance is still running as a standby at that point
- SCOPE=BOTH changes memory immediately - so DEST_2 is deferred before the activation converts the instance to primary
- It also persists in spfile so it survives any subsequent restart
- SCOPE=SPFILE alone would NOT defer DEST_2 in memory - the error would still occur immediately after activation

# 23\. Rebuild Failed Primary as New Standby

## 23.1 Option A - Reinstate via Flashback Database (Preferred)

We use **Option A - Reinstate via Flashback Database** since Flashback was enabled on lnx107 before the failover.

### 23.1.1 Check Flashback SCN on New Primary (lnx113)

\-- On lnx113 as oracle - Check Flashback SCN o

sqlplus / as sysdba

\-- Get the SCN at which failover occurred

\-- lnx107 must be flashed back to a point BEFORE this SCN

\-- On lnx113

SELECT TO_CHAR(STANDBY_BECAME_PRIMARY_SCN) AS FAILOVER_SCN

FROM V\$DATABASE;

**\# 23.1.1 lnx113**

SQL> SELECT TO_CHAR(STANDBY_BECAME_PRIMARY_SCN) AS FAILOVER_SCN

FROM V\$DATABASE;

&nbsp; 2

FAILOVER_SCN

**\----------------------------------------**

3080220

\-- Note this value - needed for flashback on lnx107

### 23.1.2 Prepare lnx107 Before Starting CRS

**CRITICAL - Do this BEFORE starting CRS on lnx107 to prevent database auto-opening as PRIMARY.**

The CRS start option must be changed to MOUNT so the database does not open as PRIMARY when CRS starts. Since lnx107 is down, change the spfile directly or update via OCR after CRS starts but before database starts.

The safest approach is to start CRS with HAS only (no database), then change the start option:

\# As root on lnx107 - start CRS stack only

crsctl start crs

\# Immediately disable auto-start of database before it starts

\# Wait for CRS to come online but watch database status

crsctl check crs

\# As oracle on lnx107 - immediately after CRS comes online

\# Change start option to MOUNT before database auto-starts

srvctl modify database -d CDBPRIM -startoption MOUNT

\# If database already started as OPEN - abort it immediately

srvctl status database -d CDBPRIM

\# If running:

sqlplus / as sysdba

SHUTDOWN ABORT;

EXIT

echo "DB_UNIQUE_NAME=CDBPRIM" >> \$ORACLE_HOME/dbs/initCDBPRIM.ora

\# Start in NOMOUNT

sqlplus / as sysdba

STARTUP NOMOUNT PFILE='/u01/app/oracle/product/19.0.0/dbhome_1/dbs/initCDBPRIM.ora';

\# RMAN DUPLICATE from new primary (CDBSTBY on lnx113)

rman target sys/Oracle_4U@CDBSTBY auxiliary sys/Oracle_4U@CDBPRIM

DUPLICATE TARGET DATABASE

FOR STANDBY

FROM ACTIVE DATABASE

DORECOVER

SPFILE

PARAMETER_VALUE_CONVERT 'CDBSTBY','CDBPRIM'

SET DB_UNIQUE_NAME='CDBPRIM'

SET DB_FILE_NAME_CONVERT='+DATA/CDBSTBY','+DATA/CDBPRIM'

SET LOG_FILE_NAME_CONVERT='+DATA/CDBSTBY','+DATA/CDBPRIM'

SET FAL_SERVER='CDBSTBY'

SET FAL_CLIENT='CDBPRIM'

NOFILENAMECHECK;

\-- After RMAN DUPLICATE completes: add SRLs and start MRP

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 4 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 5 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 6 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE ADD STANDBY LOGFILE GROUP 7 ('+DATA') SIZE 200M;

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE

USING CURRENT LOGFILE DISCONNECT FROM SESSION;

# 24\. Convert Physical Standby to Snapshot Standby

A Snapshot Standby is opened READ-WRITE for testing. All local changes are discarded when converting back to physical standby via Flashback Database.

## 24.1 Prerequisites

\-- Flashback Database must be ON

SELECT FLASHBACK_ON FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- Expected: YES

\-- If not enabled:

ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK ON;

## 24.2 Convert to Snapshot Standby

\-- On standby (lnx113): stop MRP first

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE CANCEL;

\-- Convert

ALTER DATABASE CONVERT TO SNAPSHOT STANDBY;

\-- Open READ WRITE

ALTER DATABASE OPEN;

\-- Verify

SELECT DB_UNIQUE_NAME, DATABASE_ROLE, OPEN_MODE FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- Expected: CDBSTBY | SNAPSHOT STANDBY | READ WRITE

## 24.3 Convert Back to Physical Standby

\-- All local changes will be DISCARDED (Flashback restores the standby)

SHUTDOWN IMMEDIATE;

STARTUP MOUNT;

ALTER DATABASE CONVERT TO PHYSICAL STANDBY;

SHUTDOWN IMMEDIATE;

STARTUP MOUNT;

\-- Restart MRP

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE

USING CURRENT LOGFILE DISCONNECT FROM SESSION;

\-- Verify

SELECT DB_UNIQUE_NAME, DATABASE_ROLE, OPEN_MODE FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- Expected: CDBSTBY | PHYSICAL STANDBY | MOUNTED

# 25\. Configure Data Guard Broker

Data Guard Broker automates DG management, monitoring, and role transitions. It uses the DMON background process on each member and is administered via the dgmgrl command-line interface.

## 25.2 Pre-Broker Requirements

### 25.2.1 Enable Flashback on Both Nodes

**🔴 CRITICAL:** Flashback Database MUST be ON on both primary and standby before configuring Broker. Without it, REINSTATE DATABASE after failover will fail with ORA-16713 timeout.

\-- On lnx107 (primary)

sqlplus / as sysdba

SELECT DB_UNIQUE_NAME, FLASHBACK_ON FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- If NO: ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK ON;

\-- On lnx113 (standby) -- must cancel MRP first if running

sqlplus / as sysdba

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE CANCEL;

ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK ON;

ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE

USING CURRENT LOGFILE DISCONNECT FROM SESSION;

\-- Verify on both nodes

SELECT DB_UNIQUE_NAME, FLASHBACK_ON FROM V\$DATABASE;

\-- Expected: YES on both

### 25.2.2 Clear LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2 on Both Nodes

\-- On lnx107

sqlplus / as sysdba

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2='' SCOPE=BOTH;

EXIT

\-- On lnx113

sqlplus / as sysdba

ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2='' SCOPE=BOTH;

EXIT

\-- WHY: Broker manages redo transport via its own mechanism.

\-- If LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2 has SERVICE= set, ADD DATABASE fails

\-- with ORA-16698: member has a LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter

\-- with SERVICE attribute set.

**\# lnx107**

SQL> ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2='' SCOPE=BOTH;

System altered.

**\# lnx113**

SQL> ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2='' SCOPE=BOTH;

System altered.

SHOW PARAMETER DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE;

## 25.4 Create Broker Configuration

\# As oracle on lnx107

dgmgrl sys/ishan123@CDBPRIM_DIRECT

\-- Create configuration using DIRECT alias (not SCAN)

\-- WHY: SCAN listener may not have static service registration.

\-- DIRECT alias points to lnx107.home.aarisha.com:1521 which

\-- uses the Grid listener.ora static SID_LIST entries.

CREATE CONFIGURATION 'DGConfig' AS

PRIMARY DATABASE IS 'CDBPRIM'

CONNECT IDENTIFIER IS CDBPRIM_DIRECT;

\-- Add standby database

ADD DATABASE 'CDBSTBY'

AS CONNECT IDENTIFIER IS CDBSTBY_DIRECT

MAINTAINED AS PHYSICAL;

\-- Enable configuration

ENABLE CONFIGURATION;

\-- Verify

SHOW CONFIGURATION;

\-- Expected:

\-- Configuration - DGConfig

\-- Protection Mode: MaxPerformance

\-- Members:

\-- CDBPRIM - Primary database

\-- CDBSTBY - Physical standby database

\-- Configuration Status: SUCCESS

## 26.2 Execute Broker Switchover

\-- Broker handles ALL steps automatically:

\-- 1. Flushes redo on primary

\-- 2. Switches primary to standby role

\-- 3. Activates standby as new primary

\-- 4. Starts MRP on old primary (now standby)

\-- 5. Opens all PDBs on new primary

\-- 6. Updates all LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST parameters automatically

SWITCHOVER TO 'CDBSTBY';

\-- Verify

SHOW CONFIGURATION;

\-- CDBSTBY should now be PRIMARY, CDBPRIM should be PHYSICAL STANDBY

## 26.5 Common Issues During Broker Switchover

| **Error**                                             | **Cause**                                              | **Fix**                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ORA-16698: member has LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n with SERVICE | LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2 still set with SERVICE= on a member | ALTER SYSTEM SET LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_2='' SCOPE=BOTH on both nodes before ADD DATABASE |
| ORA-16532: Broker configuration does not exist        | Connecting to wrong node or DMON not started           | Verify DG_BROKER_START=TRUE; connect via CDBPRIM_DIRECT not SCAN alias              |
| Transient ORA-16853: apply lag exceeded threshold     | Broker just connected and measuring lag for first time | Wait 30-60 seconds - clears automatically                                           |
| Transient ORA-16629: different protection level       | Standby catching up after switchover                   | Wait 30-60 seconds - clears automatically as redo applies                           |
| Services not auto-starting after switchover           | First switchover after services created in session     | Start manually once - AUTOMATIC policy works on subsequent switchovers              |
